accepted.question_text: Consider the controlled reaction-diffusion system for n interacting populations on the real line, with state u=(u_1,…,u_n), control α:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^m, diffusion coefficients σ_i, and traveling-wave profiles U=(U_1,…,U_n) of speed β that solve f_i(U,α)+σ_i U_i''+β U_i'=0 for i=1,…,n together with the asymptotic conditions U_i(-\infty)=u_i^- and U_i(+\infty)=u_i^+. Among all controls that produce such a traveling wave, develop a fully general theory for the optimal traveling-wave problem of minimizing the cost I(U,α)=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} L(U(x),α(x))\,dx, including general existence results and necessary conditions for optimality under broad assumptions on f and L.

evidence.quote: In the above setting, the cost functional does not admit the convenient representation (2.12). A fully general theory for this type of optimization problems is not yet available. Under suitable assumptions on the functions f and L, one can prove the existence of optimal solutions, and derive necessary conditions for optimality. Some results in this direction, valid for specific biological models, can be found in [13].

accepted.question_text: Let t→Ω(t)⊂\mathbb{R}^2 be a moving set with C^1 boundary whose inward normal speed is β(t,x)≥β^*, and let u^ε solve the rescaled controlled reaction-diffusion equation u_t^ε=(1/ε)f(u^ε)+εΔu^ε-α^ε u^ε. Suppose a family of controls α^ε≥0 and solutions u^ε satisfies the sharp-interface convergence ||u^ε(t,·)-1_{Ω(t)}||_{L^1}→0 for every t\in[0,T]. Must one then have the lower-bound inequality lim inf_{ε→0} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} α^ε(t,x)\,dx \ge \int_{∂Ω(t)} E(β(t,x))\,dσ for the effective boundary-control cost at each time? A positive answer would provide the missing converse needed to regard the moving-set cost functional as a Γ-limit of the rescaled parabolic control functionals.

evidence.quote: In view of these results, one may speculate if it is possible to regard the cost functional J as a Γ-limit of the functionals Jε. Toward this goal, one would need a converse to Theorem 3.1.

Question 1: In the same setting of Theorem 3.1, consider any family of control functions αε ≥ 0 and corresponding solutions uε to (3.6) such that (3.7) holds. Does this imply that lim inf ε→0 \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} αε(t, x) dx ≥ \int_{∂Ω(t)} E(β(t, x)) dσ ? (3.10)

accepted.question_text: For the optimal set motion problem (OSM), where one minimizes J(u)=Ψ(u)+κ_1\int_0^T\int u(t,x)\,dxdt+κ_2\int u(T,x)\,dx over indicator-valued BV evolutions of sets Ω(t)⊂\mathbb{R}^2 with a cost Ψ(u) induced by the effort function E and the projected surface measure of the moving boundary, establish regularity of an optimal set-valued solution t→Ω(t). In particular, prove enough regularity of the evolving boundaries ∂Ω(t) to ensure that orthogonal trajectories to these boundaries are well defined, so that the Pontryagin-type necessary conditions derived under the C^{1,1} parametrization assumption become applicable to actual optimal solutions.

evidence.quote: At this stage, we must point out that a major gap still remains in the theory. Indeed, Theorem 4.1 yields the existence of optimal solutions t → Ω(t) within a general class of sets with finite perimeter. On the other hand, the necessary conditions require a much stronger regularity assumption.
Problem 2. Establish the regularity of the set valued map t → Ω(t) which provides a solution to (OSM). In particular, prove that the orthogonal curves to the boundaries ∂Ω(t) are well defined.

accepted.question_text: Let V⊂\mathbb{R}^2 be a bounded open connected domain with bounded perimeter, and consider the constrained eradication problem in which a contaminated region Ω(t)⊂V evolves under the effort law E(β)=max{1+β,0} and a total available effort bound M applied only along the relative boundary ∂Ω(t)∩V. Describe the optimal strategy t→Ω(t) that drives Ω(T)=∅ in minimum time for general V, especially when V is a polygon or when V is a convex domain with smooth boundary.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Given an open connected domain V ⊂ R2 with bounded perimeter, describe the optimal strategy t → Ω(t) ⊂ V for (CEP), achieving the eradication in minimum time. In particular, it would be of interest to study the cases where (i) V is a polygon, or (ii) V is a convex set with smooth boundary.

accepted.question_text: Let V⊂\mathbb{R}^2 be a compact connected set of area A. Find a nested family of subsets t→Ω(t)⊂V for t\in[0,A] such that m_2(Ω(t))=t, Ω(t_1)⊂Ω(t_2) whenever 0≤t_1<t_2≤A, and the average relative-boundary length \int_0^A m_1(V∩∂Ω(t))\,dt is minimized. Determine the optimal slicing in geometric situations not covered by the sufficient conditions discussed earlier, such as domains of the type illustrated in Figure 20.

evidence.quote: (OSP) (Optimal slicing problem). Let V ⊂ R2 be a compact connected set with m2(V ) = A > 0. Construct a family of sets t → Ω(t) ⊂ V whose relative boundaries minimize the integral ∫ A 0 m1(V ∩ ∂Ω(t)) dt, subject to m2(Ω(t)) = t, for all t ∈ [0, A], Ω(t1) ⊂ Ω(t2), for 0 ≤ t1 < t2 ≤ A.
It remains an open problem to understand the optimal slicing of a set such as the one in Fig. 20.
